title: Non-Appearance, Withdrawal and Reopening Terms for Unemployment Insurance Appeals
content:
What happens when the appellant does not appear, what happens when only the other party is absent, how long a dismissed appellant has to ask for reopening, and how late an appellant may withdraw: each docket of Unemployment Insurance Appeals fixes these terms as follows. The reopening request period is counted in calendar days after the dismissal is mailed.

| Docket | Result when the appellant does not appear | Result when only the other party does not appear | Reopening request period (calendar days after the dismissal is mailed) | Good cause required for reopening | Good cause and merits heard at the same hearing | Appellant may withdraw until |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lower Authority Appeal — Separation Issue | dismissal | decision on the evidence presented | 15 | yes | yes | the decision is issued |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Able and Available Issue | dismissal | decision on the evidence presented | 15 | yes | yes | the decision is issued |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Monetary Determination | dismissal | decision on the evidence presented | 15 | yes | yes | the decision is issued |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Overpayment and Fraud | dismissal | decision on the evidence presented | 15 | yes | yes | the decision is issued |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Employer Benefit Charge | dismissal | decision on the evidence presented | 15 | yes | yes | the decision is issued |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Employer Contribution Rate | dismissal | decision on the evidence presented | 15 | yes | yes | the decision is issued |
| Higher Authority Appeal — Board of Review | not applicable (no hearing) | decision on the evidence presented | 15 | yes | no | the decision is issued |

## Reading the terms

- The reopening request period is 15 calendar days on every docket, and reopening always requires good cause for the missed hearing or the late filing.
- On the six lower-authority dockets good cause for reopening and the merits are heard together at one hearing; on the Board of Review they are not.
- On every docket the appellant may withdraw up to the issue of the decision and not after it.
